**Application** means a written request for membership submitted in accordance with clause 4.

**3. General Principles**

3.1 Membership of the Association is voluntary. No person is required to become a Member as a condition of their tenancy.

3.2 Membership is personal to the Member. It cannot be transferred, assigned, or inherited.

3.3 The Association is committed to ensuring that its membership procedures are fair, transparent, and applied consistently to all Applicants and Members.

3.4 The BMC is responsible for the administration of this Policy. The BMC may delegate day-to-day administrative functions to the Secretary or other officers of the Association, but the BMC retains final authority for decisions on eligibility and membership status.

3.5 Nothing in this Policy confers on any person a right to occupy premises or a right to any particular tenancy arrangement.

**4. Application Process**

The Tenant Association's membership_eligibility_policy_version is v3.2. Record status: current.

4.1 An Application must be made in writing to the Secretary of the Association. Applications may be submitted by email or by completing a paper form available from the property management office.

4.2 An Application must include the following information:

- the Applicant's full name and contact details;
- the address of the premises the Applicant occupies;
- the name of the tenant(s) listed on the tenancy agreement for those premises;
- the start date of the tenancy agreement; and
- a declaration that the information provided is true and correct.

4.3 The Secretary will acknowledge receipt of an Application within five (5) business days.

4.4 The Secretary will assess the Application against the eligibility criteria set out in clause 5. The Secretary may request further information from the Applicant if the information provided is incomplete or unclear. The Applicant will be given a reasonable period, not less than ten (10) business days, to provide the requested information.

4.5 Following the assessment, the Secretary will recommend to the BMC either that the Application be approved or that it be refused. The BMC will consider the recommendation and make a decision at its next scheduled meeting, or earlier if the matter is urgent.

4.6 The Secretary will notify the Applicant in writing of the BMC's decision within five (5) business days of the decision being made. Where an Application is refused, the notice will include the reasons for the refusal.

4.7 An Applicant whose Application is refused may request a review of the decision. A request for review must be made in writing to the BMC within fourteen (14) days of receiving the notice of refusal. The BMC will conduct the review and notify the Applicant of the outcome within twenty-one (21) days of receiving the request.

**5. Eligibility Criteria**

5.1 To be eligible for membership, an Applicant must satisfy all of the following criteria at the date of their Application:

- the Applicant is a Tenant as defined in clause 2;
- the Applicant is at least eighteen (18) years of age;
- the Applicant has not been found by the BMC to have breached this Policy or the Association's Constitution on more than one occasion in the preceding two (2) years; and
- the Applicant is not currently suspended from membership of the Association.
- holidays or travel, whether within Australia or overseas;
- periods of hospitalisation or medical treatment;
- a period of temporary relocation for work or study, provided the Applicant intends to return to the premises as their principal place of residence; or
- any other absence of a similar nature that the Secretary determines to be consistent with a continuing intention to reside at the premises.

5.7 An Applicant who relies on a temporary absence under clause 5.6 must disclose the absence in their Application and provide a brief explanation of its nature and duration. The Secretary may request supporting documentation, including travel itineraries, medical certificates, or a letter from an employer or educational institution. Failure to disclose a temporary absence may result in the Application being refused.

5.8 The BMC may, in its absolute discretion, waive the residency requirement in whole or in part where it is satisfied that exceptional circumstances exist. Exceptional circumstances may include, but are not limited to, a prolonged absence due to the Applicant's own serious illness or that of an immediate family member, a period of required deployment with the Australian Defence Force, or a period of absence occasioned by the Applicant's need to provide care to a relative. A request for a waiver must be made in writing and lodged with the Secretary at the same time as the Application.

5.9 A waiver granted under clause 5.8 will be recorded in the minutes of the BMC meeting at which it is granted and will apply only to the Application in respect of which it was sought. A waiver does not constitute a precedent for any future Application, and each request will be considered on its own merits.

5.10 The Secretary will maintain a register of waivers granted under clause 5.8. The register will record the name of the Applicant, the lot number, the reason for the waiver, and the date of the BMC decision. The register will be available for inspection by members of the Association upon request to the Secretary.

This requirement may be amended from time to time by resolution of the Association in general meeting, and the Secretary will publish any amendment on the Association's noticeboard and by email to members.

6.1 The annual membership fee is payable by each member upon admission to membership and thereafter on each anniversary of admission. The fee is set by resolution of the Association in general meeting and is currently forty dollars ($40.00) per annum.

6.3 The Secretary will issue a receipt for each fee payment. A member who has not paid the annual fee within thirty (30) days of the due date will be notified in writing and will cease to be in good standing until payment is received. ### 9.0 Application Procedures

(a) Subject to clause 9.1, an application for membership must be made on the prescribed form (Form A – Application for Membership), which is available:

> (i) from the Estate Office during business hours (Monday to Friday, 9:00 am to 5:00 pm, excluding public holidays);

(b) The application form and all supporting documents must be submitted together. An applicant who submits an incomplete application will be notified in writing of the deficiency and may resubmit a completed application within fourteen (14) days of the date of the notification. If the applicant fails to resubmit within this period, the application will be deemed withdrawn.

(c) A separate application is required for each person seeking membership. Joint applications for a single household are not accepted, except as provided in clause 8.3(b) of this Policy for a couple residing at the same address.

(a) Applications for membership may be submitted at any time during the year.

## 10. Appeals and Disputes

### 10.1 Right of Appeal

(a) An applicant who is refused membership, or whose application is deferred under clause 9.4, may appeal that decision in accordance with this clause 10.

(b) A Member who is suspended, expelled, or whose membership is otherwise terminated under clause 11 may also appeal that decision in accordance with this clause 10.

(c) An appeal under this clause must be lodged in writing with the Secretary within twenty-one (21) days of the date on which the decision being appealed was communicated to the applicant or Member (as the case may be).

(d) The written notice of appeal must:

> (i) state the name and contact details of the appellant;

> (ii) identify the decision being appealed and the date of that decision;

> (iii) set out the grounds of the appeal in sufficient detail to allow the Committee to understand the basis of the appeal; and

> (iv) be signed and dated by the appellant.

(e) An appeal lodged after the period specified in clause 10.1(c) will not be accepted unless the Committee, in its absolute discretion, determines that there are exceptional circumstances justifying the late lodgement. Any request for an extension of time must be made in writing and must accompany the notice of appeal.

### 10.2 Preliminary Review by the Secretary

(a) Upon receipt of a notice of appeal, the Secretary will:

> (i) acknowledge receipt of the appeal in writing within five (5) business days;

> (ii) review the notice to confirm that it complies with clause 10.1(d); and

> (iii) compile the relevant records, including the original application (if any), the decision under appeal, and any correspondence between the Association and the appellant.

(b) If the Secretary determines that the notice of appeal is incomplete, the Secretary will notify the appellant in writing of the specific information required. The appellant will have ten (10) business days from the date of that notification to provide the required information. If the appellant fails to provide the required information within that period, the appeal will be deemed to have been withdrawn.

(c) The Secretary will refer the completed appeal, together with the compiled records, to the Committee within ten (10) business days of the date on which the appeal is deemed complete.

### 10.3 Review by the Committee

(a) The Committee will consider the appeal at its next scheduled meeting, provided that the appeal has been referred to the Committee at least seven (7) days before that meeting. If the appeal is referred less than seven (7) days before the next scheduled meeting, the Committee will consider the appeal at the meeting following that one.

(b) In considering the appeal, the Committee may:

> (i) affirm the original decision;

> (ii) vary the original decision;

> (iii) set aside the original decision and substitute a new decision; or

> (iv) refer the matter back to the original decision-maker for reconsideration, with or without directions.

(c) The Committee may request further information from the appellant or from any other person it considers relevant. Any such request will be made in writing, and the appellant will be given a reasonable opportunity to respond.

(d) The Committee may, but is not obliged to, offer the appellant an opportunity to make oral submissions to the Committee. Where oral submissions are offered, the appellant may be accompanied by a support person, but may not be legally represented unless the Committee, in its discretion, permits legal representation in the particular circumstances of the case.
## 11. Policy Review and Amendments

### 11.1 Annual Review

(a) The Committee will undertake a comprehensive review of this Policy at least once in each calendar year, ordinarily during the month of June, so that any amendments may take effect from 1 July.

(b) The purpose of the annual review is to ensure that the Policy:

> (i) remains consistent with the Objects of the Association and the By-laws;

> (ii) reflects current legislative requirements, including the *Strata Schemes Management Act 2015* (NSW) and the *Associations Incorporation Act 2009* (NSW), as applicable;

> (iii) addresses any operational difficulties or ambiguities identified during the preceding year; and

> (iv) continues to serve the interests of the membership as a whole.

(c) In conducting the annual review, the Committee will have regard to:

> (i) feedback received from members during the year, whether formal or informal;

> (ii) reports from the Secretary concerning the administration of membership applications and renewals;

> (iii) any decisions made under the appeals process set out in Part 10; and

> (iv) changes to the lease arrangements at Harbourview, including any new or expiring head leases that may affect eligibility under clause 4.

(d) Following the annual review, the Committee will report to the general meeting of members on any proposed amendments, together with a brief explanation of the reasons for each proposal.

### 11.2 Proposing Amendments

(a) Any member may propose an amendment to this Policy. A proposal must be:

> (i) in writing;

> (ii) signed by the member proposing the amendment; and

> (iii) lodged with the Secretary at least twenty-one (21) days before the general meeting at which the proposal is to be considered.

(b) A proposal must set out:

> (i) the clause or clauses to which the amendment relates;

> (ii) the precise wording of the proposed amendment; and

> (iii) the reasons for the amendment.

(c) The Committee may also propose amendments to this Policy on its own motion. Where the Committee proposes an amendment, it will provide the same information required of a member under clause 11.2(b) to the Secretary, who will circulate the proposal in accordance with clause 11.3.

(d) A proposal that is frivolous, vexatious, or otherwise not made in good faith may be ruled out of order by the Chair of the meeting at which it is to be considered. The Chair's ruling is final.

### 11.3 Circulation of Proposed Amendments

(a) The Secretary will circulate any proposed amendment to all members, together with the notice of the general meeting at which the amendment will be considered, in accordance with the notice requirements of the By-laws.

(b) The circulation will include:

> (i) the full text of the proposed amendment;

> (ii) a statement of the reasons for the amendment; and

> (iii) where the amendment has been proposed by a member, the name of that member.

### 11.4 Approval Process

(a) An amendment to this Policy will be approved only if it is passed by a resolution of a general meeting of members.

(b) A resolution to amend this Policy requires a two-thirds majority of the votes cast by members present and eligible to vote at the meeting, whether in person, by proxy, or by electronic means where such means have been adopted by the Association.

**3. General Principles**

3.1 Membership of the Association is voluntary. No person is required to become a Member as a condition of their tenancy.

3.2 Membership is personal to the Member. It cannot be transferred, assigned, or inherited.

3.3 The Association is committed to ensuring that its membership procedures are fair, transparent, and applied consistently to all Applicants and Members.

3.4 The BMC is responsible for the administration of this Policy. The BMC may delegate day-to-day administrative functions to the Secretary or other officers of the Association, but the BMC retains final authority for decisions on eligibility and membership status.

3.5 Nothing in this Policy confers on any person a right to occupy premises or a right to any particular tenancy arrangement.

**4. Application Process**

The Tenant Association's membership_eligibility_policy_version is v3.2. Record status: current.

4.1 An Application must be made in writing to the Secretary of the Association. Applications may be submitted by email or by completing a paper form available from the property management office.

4.2 An Application must include the following information:

- the Applicant's full name and contact details;
- the address of the premises the Applicant occupies;
- the name of the tenant(s) listed on the tenancy agreement for those premises;
- the start date of the tenancy agreement; and
- a declaration that the information provided is true and correct.

4.3 The Secretary will acknowledge receipt of an Application within five (5) business days.

4.4 The Secretary will assess the Application against the eligibility criteria set out in clause 5. The Secretary may request further information from the Applicant if the information provided is incomplete or unclear. The Applicant will be given a reasonable period, not less than ten (10) business days, to provide the requested information.

4.5 Following the assessment, the Secretary will recommend to the BMC either that the Application be approved or that it be refused. The BMC will consider the recommendation and make a decision at its next scheduled meeting, or earlier if the matter is urgent.

4.6 The Secretary will notify the Applicant in writing of the BMC's decision within five (5) business days of the decision being made. Where an Application is refused, the notice will include the reasons for the refusal.

4.7 An Applicant whose Application is refused may request a review of the decision. A request for review must be made in writing to the BMC within fourteen (14) days of receiving the notice of refusal. The BMC will conduct the review and notify the Applicant of the outcome within twenty-one (21) days of receiving the request.

5.1 To be eligible for membership, an Applicant must satisfy all of the following criteria at the date of their Application:

- the Applicant is a Tenant as defined in clause 2;
- the Applicant is at least eighteen (18) years of age;
- the Applicant has not been found by the BMC to have breached this Policy or the Association's Constitution on more than one occasion in the preceding two (2) years; and
- the Applicant is not currently suspended from membership of the Association.

(b) "continuous period" means a period of occupation without interruption, whether under one agreement or a series of successive agreements with no gap in occupation;

(c) a lease is taken to have commenced on the date the Applicant was first entitled to occupy the Lot under the agreement, regardless of the date on which the Applicant actually moved in;

(d) a lease is taken to have ended on the date the Applicant's right to occupy the Lot ceased, regardless of any period of notice given or rent paid in lieu of notice.

(c) A separate application is required for each person seeking membership. Joint applications for a single household are not accepted, except as provided in clause 8.3(b) of this Policy for a couple residing at the same address.

### 9.1 Supporting Documents

(a) An applicant must provide the following documents with their application:

> (i) proof of identity, being a current Australian driver licence, passport, or proof of age card;

> (ii) proof of residence at the Estate, being one of the following:

>> (A) a current residential tenancy agreement in the applicant's name;

>> (B) a current strata title or certificate of title showing the applicant as owner or co-owner of a lot within the Estate;

> (iv) if the applicant is applying as a concession card holder under clause 8.7(a)(iii), a current concession card issued by Centrelink or the Department of Veterans' Affairs, showing the applicant's name.

## 10. Appeals and Disputes

### 10.1 Right of Appeal

(a) An applicant who is refused membership, or whose application is deferred under clause 9.4, may appeal that decision in accordance with this clause 10.

(b) A Member who is suspended, expelled, or whose membership is otherwise terminated under clause 11 may also appeal that decision in accordance with this clause 10.

(c) An appeal under this clause must be lodged in writing with the Secretary within twenty-one (21) days of the date on which the decision being appealed was communicated to the applicant or Member (as the case may be).

(d) The written notice of appeal must:

> (i) state the name and contact details of the appellant;

> (ii) identify the decision being appealed and the date of that decision;

> (iii) set out the grounds of the appeal in sufficient detail to allow the Committee to understand the basis of the appeal; and

> (iv) be signed and dated by the appellant.

(e) An appeal lodged after the period specified in clause 10.1(c) will not be accepted unless the Committee, in its absolute discretion, determines that there are exceptional circumstances justifying the late lodgement. Any request for an extension of time must be made in writing and must accompany the notice of appeal.

### 10.2 Preliminary Review by the Secretary

(a) Upon receipt of a notice of appeal, the Secretary will:

> (i) acknowledge receipt of the appeal in writing within five (5) business days;

> (ii) review the notice to confirm that it complies with clause 10.1(d); and

> (iii) compile the relevant records, including the original application (if any), the decision under appeal, and any correspondence between the Association and the appellant.

(b) If the Secretary determines that the notice of appeal is incomplete, the Secretary will notify the appellant in writing of the specific information required. The appellant will have ten (10) business days from the date of that notification to provide the required information. If the appellant fails to provide the required information within that period, the appeal will be deemed to have been withdrawn.

(c) The Secretary will refer the completed appeal, together with the compiled records, to the Committee within ten (10) business days of the date on which the appeal is deemed complete.

### 10.3 Review by the Committee

(a) The Committee will consider the appeal at its next scheduled meeting, provided that the appeal has been referred to the Committee at least seven (7) days before that meeting. If the appeal is referred less than seven (7) days before the next scheduled meeting, the Committee will consider the appeal at the meeting following that one.

(b) In considering the appeal, the Committee may:

> (i) affirm the original decision;

> (ii) vary the original decision;

> (iii) set aside the original decision and substitute a new decision; or

> (iv) refer the matter back to the original decision-maker for reconsideration, with or without directions.

(c) The Committee may request further information from the appellant or from any other person it considers relevant. Any such request will be made in writing, and the appellant will be given a reasonable opportunity to respond.

(d) The Committee may, but is not obliged to, offer the appellant an opportunity to make oral submissions to the Committee. Where oral submissions are offered, the appellant may be accompanied by a support person, but may not be legally represented unless the Committee, in its discretion, permits legal representation in the particular circumstances of the case.

## 11. Policy Review and Amendments

### 11.1 Annual Review

(a) The Committee will undertake a comprehensive review of this Policy at least once in each calendar year, ordinarily during the month of June, so that any amendments may take effect from 1 July.

(b) The purpose of the annual review is to ensure that the Policy:

> (i) remains consistent with the Objects of the Association and the By-laws;

> (ii) reflects current legislative requirements, including the *Strata Schemes Management Act 2015* (NSW) and the *Associations Incorporation Act 2009* (NSW), as applicable;

> (iii) addresses any operational difficulties or ambiguities identified during the preceding year; and

> (iv) continues to serve the interests of the membership as a whole.

(c) In conducting the annual review, the Committee will have regard to:

> (i) feedback received from members during the year, whether formal or informal;

> (ii) reports from the Secretary concerning the administration of membership applications and renewals;

> (iii) any decisions made under the appeals process set out in Part 10; and

> (iv) changes to the lease arrangements at Harbourview, including any new or expiring head leases that may affect eligibility under clause 4.

(d) Following the annual review, the Committee will report to the general meeting of members on any proposed amendments, together with a brief explanation of the reasons for each proposal.

### 11.2 Proposing Amendments

(a) Any member may propose an amendment to this Policy. A proposal must be:

> (i) in writing;

> (ii) signed by the member proposing the amendment; and

> (iii) lodged with the Secretary at least twenty-one (21) days before the general meeting at which the proposal is to be considered.

(b) A proposal must set out:

> (i) the clause or clauses to which the amendment relates;

> (ii) the precise wording of the proposed amendment; and

> (iii) the reasons for the amendment.

(c) The Committee may also propose amendments to this Policy on its own motion. Where the Committee proposes an amendment, it will provide the same information required of a member under clause 11.2(b) to the Secretary, who will circulate the proposal in accordance with clause 11.3.

(d) A proposal that is frivolous, vexatious, or otherwise not made in good faith may be ruled out of order by the Chair of the meeting at which it is to be considered. The Chair's ruling is final.

### 11.3 Circulation of Proposed Amendments

(a) The Secretary will circulate any proposed amendment to all members, together with the notice of the general meeting at which the amendment will be considered, in accordance with the notice requirements of the By-laws.

(b) The circulation will include:

> (i) the full text of the proposed amendment;

> (ii) a statement of the reasons for the amendment; and

> (iii) where the amendment has been proposed by a member, the name of that member.

### 11.4 Approval Process

(a) An amendment to this Policy will be approved only if it is passed by a resolution of a general meeting of members.

(b) A resolution to amend this Policy requires a two-thirds majority of the votes cast by members present and eligible to vote at the meeting, whether in person, by proxy, or by electronic means where such means have been adopted by the Association.

(c) A quorum for a meeting at which an amendment to this Policy is to be considered will be the quorum required by the By-laws for a general meeting.
